claims.text: Cu or Zn can serve as a ductile dopant for MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials at 1–2 at%.
Adding 1–2 at% Cu or Zn will change the grain-boundary composition and microstructure of MnNiSi-based materials.
The dopant-induced grain-boundary changes will inhibit grain-boundary migration.
The dopant-induced grain-boundary changes will inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
Inhibiting grain-boundary migration and sliding will improve the mechanical properties of the doped material.
Doping will increase toughness by 20–30% relative to undoped MnNiSi-based material.
Doping will increase strength by 10–20% relative to undoped MnNiSi-based material.
A small Cu or Zn addition will minimally disrupt magnetic ordering in MnNiSi-based materials.
The doped material will retain a magnetocaloric entropy change of at least approximately 4–6 J·kg^-1·K^-1 under a 5 T field change.
Keeping the ductile-element content below 5 at% will avoid significant degradation of the magnetocaloric effect.
The magnitude of the mechanical improvement and magnetocaloric retention will depend on dopant identity, concentration, and processing conditions.
Doped and undoped MnNiSi-based specimens should be compared using toughness, strength, and magnetocaloric entropy-change measurements.
A decrease in either toughness or strength in the doped material is designated as a falsifying result.
A doped-material entropy change below 2 J·kg^-1·K^-1 under a 5 T field change is designated as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires a 20–30% toughness gain and a 10–20% strength gain, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis when either property decreases. No change or a gain below the predicted range would fail the quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.

The prediction defines retained magnetocaloric performance as approximately 4–6 J·kg^-1·K^-1 or greater at 5 T, whereas falsification requires a value below 2 J·kg^-1·K^-1. Results between 2 and the claimed retention threshold would violate the prediction but would not falsify it under the stated rule.
